## Assembly Structure and Officers
The Assembly has 31 elected Delegates. The Speaker of Benches leads and votes only to break ties.
The Clerk of the Roll keeps the Ledger of Bills. The Provost of Finance certifies any bill that spends money from the Activity Chest.
A quorum is 20 Delegates present. If a quorum call fails twice in one session, the Speaker must adjourn.
Any Delegate may introduce a bill by filing 3 typed copies with the Clerk before 8:15 a.m. on a Tuesday. The Clerk assigns a number starting with "BA" and the session year, like BA-24-07.
Every bill needs a Sponsor and at least 2 Seconders. The Clerk reads the title aloud at the first session after filing; this is the First Reading. No debate happens then.
The Speaker sends each bill to one of four committees: Grounds (7), Clubs (7), Chest (9), Rules (8). A bill spending more than 40 Silver Marks must go to the Committee on the Chest.
Key: 31 Delegates; Speaker votes only to break ties.
Key: Quorum = 20; two failed quorum calls force adjournment.
Key: File 3 copies by Tuesday 8:15 a.m.; number like BA-24-07.
Key: Sponsor + 2 Seconders; First Reading is title only, no debate.
Key: Committees: Grounds 7, Clubs 7, Chest 9, Rules 8; >40 Silver Marks → Chest.
Q: How many Delegates are in the Assembly? A: 31. The Assembly has 31 elected Delegates, so 31 is right.
Q: When may the Speaker of Benches vote? A: Only to break ties. The Speaker may vote only to break ties, so that's the right choice.
Q: What is the minimum number of Delegates present for a quorum? A: 20. A quorum is 20 Delegates present, so 20 is correct.
Q: What must the Speaker do if a quorum call fails twice in one session? A: adjourn. The Speaker must adjourn, as the passage says.
Q: A Delegate files a bill on Tuesday at 8:00 a.m. How many typed copies must they file? A: 3. The rule says three typed copies, so 3 is right.
Q: A bill spends 50 Silver Marks. Which committee must it go to? A: Committee on the Chest. Spending more than 40 Silver Marks sends it to the Chest committee.
Q: What is the prefix for a bill number assigned in session year 24? A: BA. The prefix is "BA" followed by the session year.
Q: During the First Reading, what does the Clerk do? A: Reads the title aloud. The Clerk reads the title aloud at the First Reading; no debate occurs.
Q: A bill needs a Sponsor and at least how many Seconders? A: 2. It needs at least two Seconders, so 2 is right.

## Introducing a Bill
Any Delegate may introduce a bill. They file three typed copies with the Clerk of the Roll before 8:15 a.m. on a Tuesday.
The Clerk gives each bill a number. The number starts with "BA" and then the session year, like BA-24-07.
Every bill needs a Sponsor and at least two Seconders. The Sponsor is the main person behind the bill. Seconders are others who support it.
The Clerk reads the bill's title aloud at the first session after filing. That is the First Reading. No debate happens at the First Reading.
After the First Reading, the Speaker sends the bill to a committee. There are four committees: Grounds, Clubs, Chest, and Rules.
A bill that spends more than forty Silver Marks must go to the Committee on the Chest. That committee has nine members.
Key: File 3 typed copies with the Clerk before 8:15 a.m. on a Tuesday.
Key: Bill number: BA + session year (e.g., BA-24-07).
Key: Need 1 Sponsor and at least 2 Seconders.
Key: First Reading: Clerk reads title aloud; no debate.
Key: Speaker refers bill to a committee; spending >40 Silver Marks goes to Committee on the Chest.
Q: How many typed copies of a bill must a Delegate file? A: Three. The rule says three typed copies, so three is the right number.
Q: What is the prefix for a bill number? A: BA. The prefix is BA, as in BA-24-07.
Q: What is the minimum number of Seconders a bill must have? A: two. The rule says at least two Seconders.
Q: A bill is filed on Tuesday. When does the First Reading happen? A: At the first session after filing. The Clerk reads the title at the first session after filing, so that is the First Reading.
Q: A bill spends 50 Silver Marks. Which committee must it go to? A: Committee on the Chest. Spending more than 40 Silver Marks means it must go to the Committee on the Chest.
Q: What is the name of the officer who keeps the Ledger of Bills? A: Clerk of the Roll. The Clerk of the Roll keeps the Ledger of Bills.
Q: A Delegate files a bill on Tuesday. What happens at the First Reading? A: The title is read aloud. At the First Reading, the Clerk reads the title aloud and no debate occurs.
Q: A bill spends 30 Silver Marks. Which committee can it go to? A: Any of the four committees. Since it spends 30 (not more than 40), it does not have to go to the Chest, so the Speaker can refer it to any committee.

## Committee Review
A bill starts with a First Reading, then goes to a committee.
The Speaker sends each bill to one of four committees.
A bill that spends more than 40 Silver Marks must go to the Committee on the Chest.
Committees meet on Thursday in Room 114. A committee quorum is 5 members.
A committee can report the bill Favorably, with Amendments, table it, or kill it by a two-thirds vote.
After committee, the bill gets a Second Reading at least 3 school days later.
Amendments are voted on one by one by show of hands before the final vote.
The Third Reading comes right after amendments. Passage needs a simple majority of Delegates present, but at least 11 yes votes.
No bill may be voted on the same day it gets its Second Reading, unless all Delegates present agree.
After passage, the Chancellor must sign, veto, or return it unsigned within 5 school days.
Key: No bill may be voted on the same day it receives its Second Reading, except by unanimous consent of all Delegates present.
Key: Amendments are voted on individually by show of hands before the final vote.
Q: What is the minimum number of Delegates present needed for a quorum in the Assembly? A: 20. A quorum is 20 Delegates present, as stated in Section 2.
Q: Which committee handles a bill that spends more than 40 Silver Marks? A: Committee on the Chest. A bill spending more than 40 Silver Marks must go to the Committee on the Chest.
Q: A committee has 6 members present. How many must vote to kill a bill? A: 4. Killing a bill needs two-thirds of members present. Two-thirds of 6 is 4.
Q: How many school days must pass between a bill's committee report and its Second Reading? A: 3. The Second Reading comes no sooner than 3 school days after the committee report.
Q: A bill gets its Second Reading on Monday. When can it be voted on? A: Monday, if all Delegates present agree. The rule says no vote on the same day as Second Reading, except by unanimous consent of all Delegates present.
Q: How are amendments voted on before the final vote? A: Individually by show of hands. Amendments are voted on individually by show of hands before the final vote.
Q: A bill passes with 10 yes votes and 5 no votes. Is it passed? A: No, because it needs 11 yes votes. Passage needs a simple majority but never fewer than 11 yes votes. 10 is too few.
Q: A bill passes on Friday. By when must the Chancellor act? A: Within 5 school days. The Chancellor must act within 5 school days of passage.
Q: A bill is in committee. What can the committee do? A: Report, amend, table, or kill it. The committee may report favorably, with amendments, table it, or kill it.

## Floor Debate and Voting
A bill gets its Second Reading at least three school days after it leaves committee. The Clerk reads the full text. Each Delegate may speak once for up to four minutes; the Sponsor may speak twice.
Amendments are voted on one by one, by show of hands, before the final vote. After all amendments are settled, the Third Reading happens right away.
Passage needs a simple majority of Delegates present, but never fewer than eleven yes votes. A simple majority means more than half of those present.
No bill may be voted on the same day it gets its Second Reading, unless every Delegate present agrees. This rule is important.
After passage, the Chancellor has five school days to act. The Chancellor may sign the bill (it becomes an Act), veto it with a written objection of up to 150 words, or do nothing for five days (it becomes an Act without a signature).
Key: Second Reading: at least 3 school days after committee report; Clerk reads full text; each Delegate speaks once (4 min max), Sponsor twice.
Key: Amendments: voted individually by show of hands before final vote; Third Reading immediately after.
Key: Passage: simple majority of Delegates present, but at least 11 yes votes.
Key: No vote on same day as Second Reading unless unanimous consent.
Key: Chancellor: sign, veto (≤150 words), or return unsigned after 5 days (becomes Act).
Q: How many school days must pass after a committee report before the Second Reading? A: Three. The rule says 'no sooner than three (3) school days later.'
Q: How are amendments voted on? A: Individually by show of hands. The material says 'Amendments are voted on individually by show of hands.'
Q: What is the minimum number of yes votes needed for passage? A: Eleven. The material says 'never fewer than eleven (11) yes votes.'
Q: A bill gets its Second Reading on Monday. When can it be voted on? A: Any later day, but not the same day. The rule says no vote on the same day as the Second Reading, unless everyone agrees.
Q: What must the Chancellor do within five school days of passage? A: Sign it, veto it, or return it unsigned. The material lists three options: sign, veto, or return unsigned after five days.
Q: A bill passes. The Chancellor does nothing for five school days. What happens? A: It becomes an Act without a signature. The material says 'return it unsigned after five days, in which case it becomes an Act without signature.'
Q: A bill is in committee. How many members must be present to have a quorum? A: Five. The material says 'A committee quorum is five (5).'
Q: A delegate wants to speak on a bill during the Second Reading. How long can they speak? A: Up to 4 minutes. The material says 'Delegates may speak once for up to four (4) minutes.'

## Executive Approval and Veto
The Chancellor is the Assembly's presiding executive, elected at large. Within five school days of passage, the Chancellor must sign the bill, veto it with a written objection of no more than 150 words, or return it unsigned after five days, in which case it becomes an Act without signature.
A vetoed bill returns to the floor at the next session. The Assembly may override the veto only by a vote of twenty-one of the thirty-one Delegates. If the override succeeds, the bill becomes an Act over the Chancellor's objection.
No bill may be voted on the same day it receives its Second Reading, except by unanimous consent of all Delegates present. This rule is important and is stressed in the material.
Amendments are voted on individually by show of hands before the final vote. The Third Reading occurs immediately after amendments are settled. Passage requires an affirmative vote of a simple majority of Delegates present, but never fewer than eleven yes votes.
An Act takes effect at 8:00 a.m. on the tenth school day after signature, unless the Act itself states a later date. Acts affecting the Activity Chest take effect only after the Provost of Finance countersigns.
The Clerk of the Roll must publish every Act on the Assembly board within two school days of effect. Any Act not published within this window is suspended until publication occurs.
Repeal of an Act follows the same path as enactment, except that the committee stage may be waived by a two-thirds floor vote. Emergency measures affecting health or safety may be introduced at any session and passed by a vote of twenty-four Delegates. Such measures expire automatically twenty school days after effect unless re-enacted under the ordinary procedure.
Key: No bill may be voted on the same day it receives its Second Reading, except by unanimous consent of all Delegates present.
Key: Amendments are voted on individually by show of hands before the final vote.
Q: What must the Chancellor do within five school days of a bill's passage? A: Sign it, veto it, or return it unsigned. The Chancellor must sign, veto, or return unsigned within five school days.
Q: How many Delegates must vote to override a veto? A: 21. The override needs 21 of the 31 Delegates.
Q: A bill receives its Second Reading on Monday. When can it be voted on? A: Tuesday, if all Delegates agree. The rule says no vote on the same day, but unanimous consent allows it.
Q: How are amendments voted on? A: Individually by show of hands. Amendments are voted on individually by show of hands.
Q: A bill passes with 10 yes votes. Is that enough? A: No, because it needs at least 11 yes votes. Passage needs a simple majority but never fewer than 11 yes votes.
Q: What happens if the Chancellor does not sign a bill within five school days? A: It becomes an Act without signature. Returning it unsigned after five days makes it an Act without signature.
Q: An Act takes effect at 8:00 a.m. on the tenth school day after signature. What if the Act states a later date? A: The later date is used. The Act takes effect on the later date if it states one.
Q: What happens if the Clerk does not publish an Act within two school days of effect? A: The Act is suspended until publication. The Act is suspended until it is published.
Q: An emergency health measure passes with 24 votes. How long does it last? A: 20 school days after effect. Emergency measures expire 20 school days after effect unless re-enacted.

## Effective Dates, Publication, and Special Procedures
A vetoed bill goes back to the floor at the next session. The Assembly can override the veto with 21 of 31 Delegates. If that happens, the bill becomes an Act anyway.
An Act takes effect at 8:00 a.m. on the 10th school day after signature, unless it says a later date. Acts that affect the Activity Chest need the Provost of Finance to countersign first.
The Clerk of the Roll must publish every Act on the Assembly board within 2 school days of effect. If not published in time, the Act is suspended until it is published.
Repealing an Act follows the same steps as making one, except the committee stage can be skipped by a two-thirds floor vote.
Emergency measures for health or safety can be introduced at any session and need 24 Delegates to pass. They expire automatically 20 school days after effect unless re-enacted the normal way.

Key: Effective date: 8:00 a.m. on 10th school day after signature, unless later date stated.

Key: Repeal: same as enactment, but committee stage can be waived by two-thirds vote.
Key: Emergency: 24 Delegates, any session, expires after 20 school days unless re-enacted.
